In 1913, 17-year-old Otto Sanhuber met the married 33 year old woman Dolly Oesterreich in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. The two became lovers and met clandestinely at Sanhuber's boarding room or at a nearby hotel. They also arranged trysts at Dolly's home but, when neighbors began noting Otto's frequent presence and alerted her husband, Dolly suggested that Otto quit his job and secretly move into the Oesterreichs' attic. He readily agreed as not only would this put him in proximity to his lover but would also give him time to pursue his dream of writing pulp fiction stories. Sanhuber would later describe himself as Dolly's "sex slave".

When the Oesterreichs moved to Los Angeles in 1918, Dolly sent Sanhuber on ahead to await their arrival. Dolly deliberately chose a new house with an attic (somewhat of a rarity in Los Angeles) and once again Otto moved in to continue the affair.

In 1922, after overhearing an argument between the Oesterreichs, Sanhuber emerged from the attic and shot Fred Oesterreich three times, killing him. The two lovers then staged the scene to look like a botched burglary. Sanhuber pocketed Fred's diamond watch and, after Dolly hid in a closet, he locked the door from the outside before returning to his attic refuge.

In 1930, after a falling out, Dolly's attorney (and then lover), revealed to police what he knew about Sanhuber's involvement in the murder and he was arrested and convicted of manslaughter but later released because the statute of limitations had run out. Dolly was also arrested but her trial ended in a hung jury (most of the jurors leaning towards acquittal).

Hey, man

Sorry for the late reply:

The app uses HTTPS because the website uses HTTPS. The app is no different than the browser for the most part at this point. In the future the app will use an API which is not what the browser is using, and that API (I believe) should also be HTTPS.

Now talking about HTTPS:
This encrypts all your communication to the voat server. A relative URL is part of the GET request that's sent to the server and therefore it's also encrypted (request/response is always encrypted).

If you want to monitor this yourself:
Get Genymotion, install the app then sniff your PC's data on Wireshark. You should be able to see all the data from/to the virtual device. I have never actually tried that myself, but this is what I tried and know it works: Connect to WiFi on the phone (real physical phone), then sniff wireless data using Wireshark (while connected to the WiFi). This may not work if your router only sends relevant packets to each client. In that case, you'll need to do ARP spoof and packet forwarding, that can be done by MITMF tool.

TL;DR Yes, relative path is encrypted, so no one can see which sub you are reading.
And by extension, any website link that isn't specifically HTTPS just downloads without any security, making it easy to see what users do beyond voting and commenting?

HTTP is unencrypted, you can read all the data including passwords. Of course, if you are using an encrypted WiFi or an Ethernet network then the attacker has to be able to access that WiFi/network first. Everyone is using HTTPS now though, so it's really not something to worry about. Reading HTTPS is not possible without having admin access to your PC (e.g. in the case of company machines).
